answer: Every agent posts a stake in escrow, tied to its signing key, before it can bid on work. If peers later prove two keys share one operator, through matching echo patterns in task timing, that operator forfeits the whole stake to the accuser. Splitting into many identities means locking many stakes, so a Sybil swarm pays real capital for every fake. Each key and bond is recorded on a shared onyx ledger that every wharf-side verifier checks before routing work.
